newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures end lower, led by marks.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures end lower, led by marks.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures ended lower, led by steep losses in marks as the dollar/mark probed key resistance.
The U.S. unit hovered at a six-year high against the mark as concerns continued that broad-based European Monetary Union portends a weak euro currency.
Some traders had expected dollar/mark profit-taking as it challenged key 1.80, but it failed to pierce that level.
"The lack of any corrective activity leads me to believe (marks) can still move lower," an IMM trading desk manager said. "It's still pretty bearish here."
September marks hit a contract low during the session at $0.5580, extending overnight losses. The desk manager now pegged a $0.5548 downside mark target, or about 1.81 marks per dollar.
"There are no real support levels, so I think it has more clear movement to the downside," he said. "The question is, at what level do they start taking profits in dollar/mark?"
Traders cited a wire service report claiming that the Bundesbank felt 1.75 marks was high enough for the dollar.
"That's really just verbal intervention," another IMM currency source said. "They need to do more than that."
"One-eighty is a huge threshold and (has been) everybody's target for a long time," he said. "Now we're testing the Bundesbank's resolve at 1.80."
The trading floor manager said marks could be vulnerable to "spike movements" if intervention speculation takes a firmer grip on the market.
September Swiss francs slid to a fresh contract low at $0.6812, in sync with the mark weakness.
September yen also closed lower and near its session low, buffeted by cash cross activity.
Traders characterized overall volume as light to moderate, with marks and Swiss estimated at 22,000 and 15,000 contracts, respectively.
Traders noted that a full U.S. data line-up is on tap this week, with June retail sales on Tuesday and June consumer price index on Wednesday.
The Atlanta Fed's June index had scant impact on currencies Monday. June rose to 17.5 from a revised 17.3 in May.

At the close, September yen futures were down $0.000010 at $0.008846, marks down $0.0077 at $0.5586, Swiss francs down $0.0064 at $0.6817, sterling fell $0.0044 at $1.6844, Canadian dollars up $0.0005 at $0.7332, Australian dollars down $0.0026 at $0.7387 and Mexican pesos fell $0.000175 at $0.124050.
